newsitem.title: USA: Frontier says United Airlines unfair.
newsitem.headline: Frontier says United Airlines unfair.

text.p: Frontier Airlines Inc President Sam Addoms alleged Thursday that UAL Corp's United Airlines was engaging in predatory practices in markets that both carriers serve.
Addoms told a press briefing that Frontier would meet next week with officials from the U.S. Justice Department and the Department of Transportation to plead its case.
Thirty-month-old Frontier operates a fleet of 10 Boeing 737 jets on routes linking its Denver hub to 14 cities in 11 states. Twelve of the routes are also served by United.
Calling United a "100-pound gorilla," Addoms said evidence it has gathered shows fares have risen in cities that Frontier has been driven out of.

For instance, charts that Frontier had at the briefing showed average fares from Denver to Billings, Mont., at $168 before Frontier started service, dropping to $92 when Frontier served the city, and rising to $208 after Frontier left.
Addoms said the public could show its displeasure with United by complaining to Congress or buying "non-United carrier products."
United said a spokesman was not immediately available but the airline would have a comment later on the Frontier allegations.
